# Blocks

Same & Different runs in blocks. Children first say whether two cards are
the same, then name the dimension two cards differ on, then pick every
card that matches a target on two, three or four dimensions. The match
blocks have no single chance level, so the below-chance check above
covers only the first two blocks.

```{r sds-blocks}
sds_block_labels <- c(same = "same", dimensions = "dimensions", `2match` = "2-match",
                      `3match` = "3-match", `4match` = "4-match")
sds <- trials |>
  filter(item_group %in% names(sds_block_labels), !is.na(correct)) |>
  mutate(block = factor(sds_block_labels[item_group], sds_block_labels),
         age_band = cut(age_at_run(run_id), c(3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 16), right = FALSE,
                        labels = c("3–4", "5–6", "7–8", "9–10", "11+"))) |>
  filter(!is.na(age_band))
# share of each dataset's first runs on its single most common score
sds_ties <- first_runs |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  summarise(n = n(), top_value = as.numeric(names(which.max(table(round(score, 3))))),
            top_share = max(table(round(score, 3))) / n(),
            top_is_max = top_value == max(round(score, 3)), .groups = "drop")
sds_top <- head(arrange(by_ds(sds_ties), desc(top_share)), 3)
```

```{r sds-blocks-plot, fig.height=3.5}
#| label: fig-sds-blocks
#| fig-cap: "Accuracy by block and age (cells with 50 or more responses)."
sds |>
  group_by(block, age_band) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 50) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_band, y = fct_rev(block), fill = accuracy)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = f2(accuracy), colour = accuracy > .5), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = NULL)
```

# Shared scores

```{r sds-ties-plot, fig.height=4}
#| label: fig-sds-ties
#| fig-cap: "Share of each dataset's first runs that have its single most common score (datasets with 50 or more runs)."
sds_ties |>
  by_ds() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = top_share, y = dataset_label, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_dataset(guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Share of runs on the most common score", y = NULL)
```

Children with the same responses get the same score. When one score
value holds a large share of a dataset's runs, the score can't tell those
children apart. The largest shares are
`r with(sds_top, paste0(dataset_labels_named[dataset], " ", fmt_pct(top_share), collapse = ", "))`.
`r tops <- filter(sds_top, top_is_max, top_share > .2); if (nrow(tops) > 0) paste0("In ", paste(dataset_labels_named[tops$dataset], collapse = " and "), " the most common score is also the highest, so those children are at the task's ceiling.") else ""`
